options.evidence: Large response can reflect strong off-resonant forcing; amplitude alone without frequency dependence and natural properties cannot establish resonance. Post-blind reconciliation: Treating noticeable amplitude as sufficient evidence deletes frequency-selectivity/natural-property checks, actually producing false A.

The absence of frequency comparison leaves resonance unresolved; controlled driving-rate comparisons related to natural response supply the missing discrimination. Post-blind reconciliation: The rationale preserves neither-confirm-nor-exclude and comparable frequency-response investigation, matching true B.

Failure to record natural frequency is absence of evidence, not proof of absence of resonance. Post-blind reconciliation: Turning missing natural-frequency data into proof of nonresonance produces false C; subsequent relevant evidence can change the assessment.

Steady forced motion follows the driving frequency even away from resonance, so rate matching alone is insufficient. Post-blind reconciliation: Substituting equality of forced response and drive frequencies for equality to natural frequency produces false D; ordinary off-resonant forcing is a counterexample.

options.evidence: A small constant force shifts the equilibrium only slightly and cannot balance the restoring force requiring 50 N at the original open position. Post-blind reconciliation: Mistaking longer constant-force duration for repeated net energy input and dynamic motion for static balance produces false A. A constant force cannot meet the 50 N holding requirement.

Correctly timed repeated forces with positive net work per cycle can increase mechanical energy and swing amplitude in the stipulated lossless linear model. Post-blind reconciliation: Continually timed positive net work under the lossless linear range supports B's gradual possible opening, not guaranteed immediate opening.

Force values omit inertia, frequency, displacement target details and the force-time protocol, so they cannot determine opening time. Post-blind reconciliation: Missing inertia, restoring/dynamic properties and force-time protocol support C's inability to determine an opening time.

Reaching a position dynamically does not reduce its static restoring force; 0.005 N still cannot supply the approximately 50 N balance there. Post-blind reconciliation: The same-position static requirement remains approximately 50 N irrespective of dynamic arrival, supporting true D.

With sufficient damping, losses balance the small drive at an amplitude below the target; timing cannot guarantee opening under arbitrary dissipation. Post-blind reconciliation: Deleting the lossless restriction allows losses to balance small-drive input before the target position, refuting E's arbitrary-dissipation guarantee.

options.evidence: A force orthogonal to the mode or applied at ineffective geometry may not excite it, even at matching frequency. Post-blind reconciliation: Dropping coupling from the resonance conditions produces A's false sufficiency claim.
